<style>
/* Layout ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
.pal{display:grid;grid-template-columns:96px repeat(9,1fr);
     border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;background:var(--bg);margin:.6rem 0}
.pal>span{display:block}
.pal .hd{font:600 10px system-ui;color:var(--fg);text-align:center;padding:8px 2px 6px;line-height:1.4}
.pal .hd em{font-style:normal;font-weight:400;opacity:.6}
.pal .rw{font:600 10px system-ui;color:var(--fg);text-align:right;padding-right:8px;align-self:center;opacity:.85}
.pal .sw{height:34px}
.pal .lc{font:11px ui-monospace,monospace;color:var(--fg);text-align:center;padding:6px 0 8px}
.pal .lc.low{color:#e06c6c}

/* Prose ------------------------------------------------------------------- */
.pr{background:var(--bg);color:var(--fg);border-radius:8px;padding:16px 18px;margin:.6rem 0;
    font-family:'Yu Gothic','Hiragino Kaku Gothic ProN',Meiryo,'MS Gothic',sans-serif}
.pr h6{font:600 9px system-ui;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;
       opacity:.55;margin:0 0 8px;border:0;padding:0}
.pr .ref{display:grid;grid-template-columns:92px 1fr;gap:2px 12px;align-items:baseline}
.pr .ref b{font:600 9px system-ui;opacity:.55;font-weight:600}
.pr p{margin:0;font-size:18px;font-weight:var(--w);line-height:1.95}
.pr .flow{font-size:17px;font-weight:var(--w);line-height:2.05}
.pr i{font-style:normal}
.ja{opacity:.55}
.pal .row{display:contents}

/* Sample sets in two columns, to cut the vertical spread. auto-fit + minmax collapses to a single
   column when the preview pane is narrow, so nothing is clipped in a split editor. */
.cols{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fit,minmax(310px,1fr));gap:10px 22px}
.cols .grp{min-width:0}
.cols .grp h6{margin-bottom:4px}

/* Consumers — declared ONCE. A palette swap is a single class change on the container, which
   redefines the --pos-* properties these rules read. */
.pronoun{color:var(--pos-pronoun)}.sw.pronoun{background:var(--pos-pronoun)}
.noun{color:var(--pos-noun)}.sw.noun{background:var(--pos-noun)}
.adnominal{color:var(--pos-adnominal)}.sw.adnominal{background:var(--pos-adnominal)}
.adjective{color:var(--pos-adjective)}.sw.adjective{background:var(--pos-adjective)}
.particle{color:var(--pos-particle)}.sw.particle{background:var(--pos-particle)}
.adverb{color:var(--pos-adverb)}.sw.adverb{background:var(--pos-adverb)}
.verb{color:var(--pos-verb)}.sw.verb{background:var(--pos-verb)}
.auxiliary{color:var(--pos-auxiliary)}.sw.auxiliary{background:var(--pos-auxiliary)}
.utterance{color:var(--pos-utterance)}.sw.utterance{background:var(--pos-utterance)}

# POS palette — candidate comparison

Candidates for the **9 part-of-speech categories** we colour, rendered against both VS Code
grounds, simulated under the three dichromacies, and measured for contrast (APCA Lc) and
perceptual separation (ΔE OK, ×100).

> Open with **Markdown: Open Preview** (`Ctrl+Shift+V`).
> Colour maths uses [colorjs.io](https://colorjs.io) (OKLCH, ΔE OK, APCA 0.1.9). CVD simulation is
> the Brettel–Viénot–Mollon linear-RGB projection, which colorjs does not ship.

## The design intent these candidates encode

Hue is **not** evenly divided across categories. It is **clustered by meaning**, so a reader parses
groups rather than nine unrelated colours:

| cluster | members | why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Things** | Pronoun · Noun | Both refer to entities — near-identical hue, so they read as one family. |
| **Actions** | Verb · Auxiliary | Auxiliaries almost always trail a verb; the pair should read as **one action unit**, placed opposite Things. |
| **Structure** | Particle | Maximally isolated from both content clusters — particles are the closest thing Japanese has to a word break. |
| **Modifiers** | Adnominal · Adjective · Adverb | Evenly divide the arc between the content clusters. |
| **Utterance** | Interjections · fillers | もしもし, ああ, おい, えと — outside the sentence skeleton, so they get their own identity. |

**Low within-cluster ΔE is a feature, not a defect.**

### Boundaries are what matter — and they are wildly uneven

A colour boundary only does work where two categories actually **touch**. Measured over the corpus
(672,371 category transitions, punctuation excluded):

| adjacent pair | share of all boundaries |
| --- | --- |
| `noun · particle` | **41.30%** |
| `particle · verb` | 18.57% |
| `auxiliary · verb` | 8.22% |
| `particle · pronoun` | 8.18% |
| `auxiliary · noun` | 5.22% |
| … 31 further pairs | 18.51% |
| `adnominal · utterance` | 0.001% (9 occurrences) |

**The top four pairs are 76% of every boundary a reader meets.** Optimising uniform separation
spends the hue wheel equally on `noun|particle` and on pairs that essentially never occur. The
recommended candidate below instead allocates separation *in proportion to* how often each pair
actually collides — and scores it under the **weakest** vision type, so no boundary can be bought
with a hue difference that vanishes under dichromacy.

### Nothing but punctuation is left uncoloured

An uncoloured word is not neutral, it is **ambiguous**: several palette colours desaturate toward
grey under dichromacy, so "no category" becomes confusable with "some category". Two classes that
previously fell through are now folded into the cluster they grammatically belong to:

| IPADIC | % of tokens | examples | folded into | why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `接頭詞` | 0.35% | **お**, 大, 新, 第 | **Noun** | Bound — never stands alone; colouring it as its host makes お宅 read as one unit. |
| `接続詞` | 0.24% | しかし, だから, 例えば | **Particle** | Joins clauses — structural, exactly what particles do. |
| `感動詞` `フィラー` | 0.14% | **もしもし**, ああ, えと | **Utterance** | Its own category (new). |

Only `記号` (punctuation, 10.3%) stays uncoloured — its glyph shape already disambiguates it.

## What the Protanopia / Deuteranopia / Tritanopia rows ARE

**They are simulations, shown to a normally-sighted viewer.** Each row answers: *"if you could see
through a dichromat's eyes, what would this palette look like?"* They are **not** alternative
palettes tuned for those viewers — every row renders the SAME nine colours, passed through the
Brettel–Viénot–Mollon transform.

So the way to read them is: **the more the CVD rows resemble the Normal row, the better the palette
is doing.** Where two swatches that differ in the Normal row become identical in the Deuteranopia
row, that pair is genuinely indistinguishable for ~6% of men — and the sentence samples show what
that does to a real sentence.

Two consequences worth being explicit about:

1. **A simulation is an approximation, not a verdict.** Dichromacy varies between individuals, and
   anomalous trichromacy (the more common condition) is a partial shift these matrices do not model.
   Feedback from people with a CVD is worth more than any number in this document.
2. **A single palette that works for everyone is not achievable at nine categories.** The measured
   ceiling is ~4 colours at full separation under deuteranopia versus 13 for normal vision (see the
   research notes). Genuinely serving CVD readers means either **separate palettes per vision type**
   — a real option, since the palette is delivered as swappable custom properties — or carrying part
   of the signal on a non-colour channel. This document deliberately shows one palette under four
   vision types so the shortfall is visible rather than assumed away.

## Reading the measurements

| metric | reading |
| --- | --- |
| **APCA Lc** | Contrast vs the background. **≥60** for body text, **≥45** for bold/large. Higher is better. |
| **ΔE cross** | Closest pair from *different* clusters — **the number to optimise**. ≥5 is comfortably distinct. |
| **ΔE within** | Mean distance *inside* each cluster. **Lower is better.** |

Frequencies measured over **76,317 sentences / 941,722 tokens** from the shipped dictionary.

---

## Summary

The two rightmost columns are **adjacency-weighted** and are the ones that predict readable word
boundaries: they score each pair by how often those categories actually sit next to each other.

| candidate | dark APCA | light APCA | ΔE within (things/actions) | weighted ΔE (**deutan**) | weakest top-5 boundary (**deutan**) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A · Figma (as authored) | 68 | 75 | 4.8 / 5.0 | **12.1** | **1.9** <span class="ja">auxiliary · noun</span> |
| E · Semantic clusters | 64 | 76 | 4.5 / 4.4 | **11.5** | **0.9** <span class="ja">auxiliary · verb</span> |
| F · Clusters + lightness offset | 60 | 71 | 9.2 / 9.0 | **13.0** | **5.6** <span class="ja">particle · verb</span> |
| G · Clusters + muted particle | 57 | 71 | 9.2 / 9.0 | **12.3** | **7.8** <span class="ja">auxiliary · verb</span> |
| J · Research-built (recommended) | 74 | 80 | 6.1 / 6.0 | **10.3** | **3.8** <span class="ja">particle · verb</span> |
| I · Adjacency-optimised | 52 | 69 | 4.0 / 10.4 | **11.3** | **9.0** <span class="ja">particle · pronoun</span> |
| H · Halation-tuned | 57 | 74 | 7.0 / 7.1 | **10.3** | **3.4** <span class="ja">particle · verb</span> |

## J · Research-built (recommended)

Rebuilt against the literature — see <a href="pos-palette-research.md">the research notes</a>. Hard accessibility constraints (CIEDE2000 ≥ 17 normal, ≥ 8 under CVD, lightness ≥ 3.9, APCA vs ground) with preference optimised <em>inside</em> the feasible region; Ström's mean-minus-range term; chroma expressed <strong>relative to each hue's gamut cusp</strong> rather than a flat value; CVD weighted by real prevalence; and nine locked basic-colour-term bands so name diversity is structural rather than emergent.

## I · Adjacency-optimised

Hue and lightness solved by simulated annealing against the corpus's real <strong>POS-adjacency matrix</strong> (672,371 transitions). Separation is maximised in proportion to how often two categories actually touch — <code>noun|particle</code> is 41.3% of all boundaries, <code>adnominal|utterance</code> is 9 — and measured under the <em>weakest</em> vision type, so no boundary can be bought with a hue difference that collapses under dichromacy. Cluster cohesion and the per-ground lightness band are hard constraints; hue is shared between grounds so a theme switch keeps the same palette.

| Particle | `助詞` + `接続詞` | 29.29% | conjunctions fold in — both are structural |
| Noun | `名詞` minus 代名詞, + `接頭詞` | ~26.8% | absorbs 形容動詞語幹, 固有名詞, and bound prefixes (お, 大) |
| Verb | `動詞` + `名詞,サ変接続`+する | 13.71% | サ変 already coalesced by the tokenizer |
| Auxiliary | `助動詞` | 10.16% | |
| Pronoun | `名詞,代名詞` | 5.06% | the one subcategory read; 6th most common overall |
| Adverb | `副詞` | 1.81% | |
| Adjective | `形容詞` | 1.51% | な-adjectives fold in, per the mind-map's ①/② model |
| Adnominal | `連体詞` | 1.38% | **new** — currently mis-coloured as adjective |
| Utterance | `感動詞` + `フィラー` | 0.14% | **new** — もしもし, ああ, えと |
| *(uncoloured)* | `記号` | 10.29% | punctuation only |

**Dropped from the original 11:** adjectival noun (な-adjectives are a subtype of adjective per the
mind-map, and IPADIC files the stem under 名詞). Conjunction and interjection were *not* dropped —
they are folded into Particle and Utterance respectively, so no word goes uncoloured.
